_doc: THE DECLARED WRITE-SET of install.sh -- every path the installer may touch OUTSIDE its
install root (${CLAUDE_HOME}), per step, with the reason. Council #12, F4: the isolation
boundary is a snapshot-diff test, not a scratch directory. install.sh --print-write-set
resolves every ${VAR} for the invocation it is given and prints this list with `active`
per entry; voidloom/tests/harness/outside_target_diff.py snapshots a $HOME before and
after a run and refuses (rc 1) on any difference this list does not name.
Inside ${CLAUDE_HOME} (memory/, skills/, commands/, hooks/) is the TARGET: what lands
there is bound by install/lay_manifest.json, not by this file. Two members of the
target root are nevertheless graded by the harness from their own before/after records
(${CLAUDE_HOME}/settings.json, ${CLAUDE_HOME}/CLAUDE.md): install.sh writes neither (except settings.json on a STEP P yes, below),
so they carry no entry here and any change to them is RED.
path syntax: exact path, or a directory followed by /** (anything beneath), or a
basename glob (tmp.*). {unit} expands to the roster's armed-by-default names.
`when` names the invocation condition; entries whose condition is false are printed
with active=false and may NOT be touched on that run.
`verbs` are the calls made to a scheduler/manager rather than writes to the
filesystem -- the HKCU class on Linux (round-1 reflection, item 3). A user manager
answers `systemctl --user enable --now` by writing under ${SYSTEMD_USER_DIR}/
timers.target.wants/ (declared above as paths, expand=armed_units), which a recorder
shim standing in for the manager never writes. So the shim's log is graded against
this list (harness verb `verbs`): every recorded call must be an active declared verb
and every active verb must have been recorded. `effect: read-only` marks a call that
reads the manager; it is declared because every call is graded, not because it writes.
SHAPES (reference-host round, R1). An entry or verb may carry `shape` (venv | tier0 | ambient): it is
active only in that install shape, which --print-write-set resolves exactly as the run does (the
--tier1-ambient flag, else <brain>/INSTALL_RECORD). `when: venv shape` marks what only the venv shape
writes (pip's wheel cache). Step R and the ambient pre-image live INSIDE the install root when the brain
is at its default path: the harness does not grade the target, but they are generated, not laid, so the
lay manifest cannot bind them -- they are declared here so that every file the installer creates that
no manifest names is named somewhere, with its reason.
THE OVERNIGHT THINKER (model-choice unit, Round 1, Wave B -- M17). Step T is the a-e answer being proven and
recorded before Step A: `when: a thinker answer` (--thinker, or an answer <brain>/THINKER_RECORD already holds --
an interactive answer cannot be known to --print-write-set, and a harness run has no terminal) and `when: a thinker
to prove` (that answer names a model: not e/off). A verb may carry `match: glob` -- its call is an fnmatch pattern,
because the probe's transient unit name and its candidate file are fresh per run; everything else in it is literal.
`untouched` lists paths the installer and every child it runs must leave BYTE-IDENTICAL: the owner's everyday
vendor logins. The harness grades each untouched path on its own (a change there is RED even if a broader
declaration would cover it).
THE PERSONA FORGE (Step P). install.sh calls install/install_persona_forge.sh after the acceptance gate passes;
it lays lay_manifest component `forge` (skills/persona-forge/, commands/persona-forge.md) under the never-
clobber contract. Its only generated writes are the *.voidloom-bak.* backups of a differing same-named item --
inside the target root, declared so every file the installer creates is named somewhere. The forge's runtime
writes (persona.json via `voidloom persona declare`, the persona_forge.declined marker via `voidloom persona
decline`, the persona's own skill folder) happen later, in a Claude Code session, at the owner's direction --
never in the installer.
STEP P ALSO ASKS whether to wire the SessionStart hook (the first-run Persona Forge offer rides it). Only a yes
-- --wire-hooks, or y at the terminal -- writes ${CLAUDE_HOME}/settings.json (`when: --wire-hooks`); otherwise
the named-member rule above holds unchanged.
THE THINKER'S PROGRAM (Gemini-thinker Round 1, lane L-I). When the answer's program is missing and the owner says yes
(--install-thinker-cli, or y to "Run it now? [y/N]"), the vendor's own installer runs before the guide's Part:
`when: an offered thinker install` (--install-thinker-cli with a CLI answer; an interactive yes cannot be known to
--print-write-set). A write carrying `backend` is active only for that answer. An `untouched` entry carrying
`unless_installing` is dropped from the list on exactly that offered install (the program's own folder is new then).

writes.why: created if absent, so the launcher symlink has a directory to live in
the `voidloom` command on PATH, pointing at ${BRAIN_DIR}/voidloom/voidloom (Step A.1d)

the brain's RESOLVED directory (os.path.realpath of ${BRAIN_DIR}): when ${BRAIN_DIR} is a symlink -- a brain kept in another directory or on another disk -- every file this install lays or writes into the brain (Steps A-E and R: the package files, the DB and its sidecars, the pre-image, the record) lands beneath the link's TARGET, outside the target root, and the link itself is unchanged; equal to ${BRAIN_DIR}, inside the target root, otherwise (env-file writer pass, iteration 4: the symlinked geometry was undeclared)

the CUDA driver's compute (JIT) cache. Written by Step A.1b-i (organs/voidloom_manifest.py write -- the hardware probe, which initialises CUDA on EVERY wet install on a host with an NVIDIA driver, --tier0-only and --force-cpu included; measured: the probe alone creates ~/.nv/ComputeCache, nvidia-smi does not) and again by the Tier-1 embed/rerank. Declared under the ALWAYS step because its writer is; absent on a host without the driver, which is permitted (a declaration is a permission, not an obligation)

SQLite WAL sidecar: the migrator writes the brain, and a read-only connection with the vec0 extension loaded materialises it beside a rollback-journal brain (measured on the fixture; the brain's bytes are unchanged by the read)
SQLite shared-memory sidecar, as above

pip's wheel cache while building the venv (the venv itself is under ${BRAIN_DIR}/venv, inside the target); pip writes under ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}, which install.sh resolves as CACHE_HOME -- the writer's rule -- the VENV shape only: the ambient shape builds no venv and runs no pip (R1)

steps.name: Tier 1 model + kernel caches (venv or ambient)

writes.why: the embedder + reranker snapshots huggingface_hub downloads at install (sizes are printed by the installer); huggingface_hub writes under ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache} when HF_HOME is unset, and the snapshot-diff harness drops HF_HOME/HF_HUB_CACHE so that is the path; in the AMBIENT shape nothing is downloaded (P3 runs with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1), but loading the cached model writes its trust_remote_code modules and lock files here (measured)

the env file's RESOLVED target (os.path.realpath): when ${ENV_FILE} is a symlink -- the reference host's geometry (R2) -- cp (never cp -f) and chmod write THROUGH it and the link itself is unchanged; equal to ${ENV_FILE} otherwise

the `claude` CLI's session transcripts land under its CONFIG dir; every thinker call gives it a per-call CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under TMPDIR (above), so on this path nothing lands here -- declared because a CLI version that ignored CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR would write here (inside the install root: bound, not graded)

steps.name: the Persona Forge (STEP P, after the acceptance gate) -- laid by install/install_persona_forge.sh, never by lay.py

writes.why: a same-named persona-forge skill folder that DIFFERS from the packaged one is moved aside here before the forge is copied (never-clobber); an identical one is left in place and nothing is written. Inside the target root: the forge files themselves are bound by install/lay_manifest.json (component forge); the backup is generated, so it is named here
the same rule for the /persona-forge command file

steps.name: STEP P's question answered yes: the SessionStart hook, so the first session offers the Persona Forge

writes.why: ONE hook element added by `voidloom hooks install --platform claude` (organs/voidloom_hooks_status.py: back-up-before, verify-after, refuse-rather-than-clobber; its receipt and pre-image live in the brain, inside the target root). Written ONLY on the owner's yes -- the --wire-hooks flag, or y at the terminal (an interactive answer cannot be known to --print-write-set). Without it install.sh never touches settings.json, and any change there is RED
mktemp for the env-file block and its rewrite; removed before exit, so a post-run snapshot must not see them

verbs.why: reload the user manager after the unit files are written (install/install_crons.sh)
arm each armed-by-default timer; the manager answers by writing ${SYSTEMD_USER_DIR}/timers.target.wants/wizard-library-{unit}.timer (declared above) and starting the timer
lists what was armed; reads the manager and writes nothing -- declared because every call the installer makes to the manager is graded, reads included
unload a previously loaded agent of the same label before re-loading it (a failure is tolerated: nothing loaded is the common case)
load the LaunchAgent; launchd registers it from ~/Library/LaunchAgents and writes no file under $HOME for it
the READ-BACK (R1): the manager's own view of every armed unit's ExecStart; its first token must be the recorded interpreter, or the run fails

the thinker's PROOF in the timers' environment (M9/M10): two tool-free calls (the exact answer to a small sum; a file that must not appear) run BY THE USER MANAGER as a transient unit (EnvironmentFile= the env file this run writes, WorkingDirectory= the brain) -- --collect removes the unit; nothing is enabled or left behind. On a host with no user manager (launchd, a container) the probe runs directly and this verb is not called

untouched.why: the owner's everyday Codex login and state: the brain signs in with its OWN CODEX_HOME (${THINKER_HOME}/codex); nothing the installer runs may read-refresh or rewrite this tree (a copied or shared auth.json refreshes itself and signs the owner out)

the owner's everyday Kimi login (credentials/kimi-code.json refreshes on an OAuth call): the brain's calls run with an EMPTY per-call KIMI_CODE_HOME and the Console key from ${THINKER_HOME}/kimi.env only

the owner's everyday Gemini / Antigravity sign-in (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token): the brain signs in with its OWN home (${THINKER_HOME}/gemini-home); nothing the installer runs may read-refresh or rewrite this tree
